dragon.name: Emberwing
dragon.title: Sovereign of Living Flame
dragon.rescueDialogue: WHOOSH! You stood firm against the magma locks! Take Bit 3—let the caverns glow with warm firelight!

trials.storyPrompt: Welcome to Cinder Cavern! Now that you know variables, an `if` statement lets Python make a decision: if a test is True, Python runs the indented code underneath! Remember two rules: put a colon `:` at the end of the `if` line, and indent the code inside by 4 spaces.
trials.objective: Start with heat = 80 and alarm = "OFF". Write an if statement: if heat > 50:, set alarm = "ON" and print("Shield up!").

starterCode.explorer:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
# Notice the colon : at the end and 4 spaces of indent below!
if heat > 50:
    alarm = "ON"
    # Now print "Shield up!" (keep the 4-space indent!)
starterCode.standard:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
# If heat > 50, set alarm = "ON" and print("Shield up!")
starterCode.challenge:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
# When heat > 50, switch alarm to "ON" and print "Shield up!".

trials.referenceSolution:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
if heat > 50:
    alarm = "ON"
    print("Shield up!")
trials.testCode:

assert OUTPUT.strip() == "Shield up!", f'Expected "Shield up!", got {OUTPUT.strip()!r}'

trials.title: Two Paths: if and else
trials.storyPrompt: What if an `if` check is False? That's where `else:` comes in! Python runs the `if` block when the test is True, and the `else:` block as the backup plan when it is False. Check your water_level box to see if the lava bridge is COOL or HOT!
trials.objective: Start with water_level = 30. Write an if / else statement: if water_level >= 50, set bridge = "COOL"; else, set bridge = "HOT". Then print(bridge).

starterCode.standard:

# Use if water_level >= 50 / else to set bridge to "COOL" or "HOT", then print(bridge)
starterCode.challenge:
water_level = 30
# Set bridge to "COOL" if water_level >= 50, otherwise "HOT", then print(bridge).

trials.testCode:
assert bridge == "HOT", f'Expected bridge == "HOT" for water_level 30, got {bridge!r}'
assert OUTPUT.strip() == "HOT", f'Expected printed "HOT", got {OUTPUT.strip()!r}'

hints.tier1_nudge: Pip fans the steam: 'Since 30 is NOT >= 50, Python skips the if block and runs the else: block!'
hints.tier3_walkthrough:
